title: Better machines only

readouts.l: Food given up per machine, first step from A

predict.q: A new method lets the same workers make **twice** as many machines. Food-growing does not change. What happens to the curve?

options.s: It shifts outward by the same amount at both ends
options.fb: A parallel shift needs both industries to improve. Farming hasn't changed, so the food end stays at 150.

options.s: It pivots outward: the machines end moves, the food end stays
options.fb: The machines end moves from 50 to 100; the food end stays at 150. Each machine now costs half as much food (1 → 0.5 tons on the first step).

options.s: The economy moves along the same curve toward machines
options.fb: A movement reallocates the same resources. Here the resources can make more, so the curve itself moves.

options.s: It shifts inward because farm workers leave for factories
options.fb: Workers moving between industries is a movement, not a loss. Better technology shifts the curve outward.

task: Move the **Machine technology** slider and watch the curve. Then compare the food given up per machine before and after.

target.do: Move the Machine technology slider to 200%, then press Check.

takeaway: A skewed outward shift. Each machine now costs **half** as much food.
